qa_pairs.question: What are the primary storage characteristics for the $HOME and $SCRATCH filesystems on the Trillium cluster, including their quotas, backup status, and accessibility on compute nodes?
qa_pairs.answer: On the Trillium cluster, the $HOME filesystem provides 100 GB and 1 million files per user, is backed up, and is available as read-only on compute nodes. The $SCRATCH filesystem offers 25 TB and 10 million files per user, is not backed up, and is fully accessible on compute nodes, though its expiration time is currently TBD.

qa_pairs.question: For the Killarney cluster, how do the storage quotas for $SCRATCH and $PROJECT filesystems differ across various user categories, and what are their respective backup and expiration policies?
qa_pairs.answer: On the Killarney cluster, $SCRATCH quotas range from 2 TB per user for CIFAR AI Chairs down to 250 GB per user for faculty members applying AI to other domains; all $SCRATCH files expire after 2 months and are not backed up. $PROJECT quotas range from 5 TB for CIFAR AI Chairs down to 500 GB for faculty members applying AI to other domains; these have no expiration time and are backed up.

qa_pairs.question: What are the distinctive backup policies and quotas for the $HOME and $PROJECT filesystems on the TamIA cluster, considering different user affiliations?
qa_pairs.answer: On the TamIA cluster, the $HOME filesystem has a 25 GB quota per user and is notably not backed up. Similarly, the $PROJECT filesystem, which offers differentiated quotas ranging from 5 TB for CIFAR AI Chairs to 500 GB for faculty members applying AI to other domains, is also not backed up. Both $HOME and $PROJECT are available on login and compute nodes.
